title: Point the agent loop at the small commands
lead: The published skill still starts on `slicer next --show --json`, edits with `--render` alone, and the long instructions point at `docs/agents.md` and never tell the model to ignore generated roadmap files.
**Not in this slice:** new pickup behavior, a merge driver, or the changelog move into `[1.0.0]`.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: `skills/slicer/SKILL.md` is generated from `ai.LOOP` and is what Claude Code, Codex, and Grok load. It tells every implementer to fetch the full slice, and `start` / `edit` use `--render` without `--require-render`, so a render failure becomes a repair turn. `slicer ai instructions` is about 6 KB and ends by linking `docs/agents.md` (about 25 KB). Nothing in that short guide says to leave `.slicer/render/ROADMAP.md` and `ROADMAP.html` unread and unmerged. Those two files are the conflict that has to be regenerated with `slicer render` after a slice merge.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/ai.py` (`LOOP` and `INSTRUCTIONS`)
- `skills/slicer/SKILL.md` (must match `ai.skill_text()`)
- `docs/agents.md` and `README.md` where they quote the loop
- `tests/test_ai.py`
- `CHANGELOG.md` under `[Unreleased]`

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `ai.LOOP`, `ai.skill_text()`, and the committed `skills/slicer/SKILL.md` name `slicer next --ready` with repeatable `--section`, `--json`, and `--lean` as the pickup. They still say to read the scope and acceptance checks before changing status.
2. The same texts use `--render --require-render` on `start` and on slice edits. `done` stays `slicer done ID --note … --render --json`.
3. `slicer ai instructions` does not send the model to `docs/agents.md` as the next read. It says not to open or hand-merge `.slicer/render/`, and to run `slicer render` then `slicer check` when those files conflict.
4. `tests/test_ai.py` matches the new sentences, including the byte-for-byte skill file check.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Rewrite the pickup sentence in `LOOP` to the bounded command from the pickup slice. Example headings are illustrations; say to pass the section names the project configures. Add `--require-render` beside `--render` for `start` and for `edit`. In `INSTRUCTIONS`, remove the "full agent reference" link to `docs/agents.md`, and add the render-file rule next to the existing "never hand-edit generated render" sentence. Keep exit-code rules, the unspecified-slice rule, and the "do not invent the section body" sentence. Regenerate the committed skill from `ai.skill_text()` rather than editing the skill by hand. Update `docs/agents.md` quotes of the loop so `tests/test_ai.py` still holds.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: The four cases above pass, `slicer ai skill` matches `skills/slicer/SKILL.md`, and `slicer check` passes. The skill file stays the short loop: it does not grow a copy of `docs/agents.md`.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit. Do not tag or push.
